company_items.summary: AutoZone reported FQ4 EPS of $56.05 versus the Street's $54.03, but the beat was low quality — driven by a 145 basis point tariff refund tailwind and a 105 basis point non-cash LIFO benefit to gross margins. Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% versus the Street's +3.1%, and the operating expense ratio rose 100 basis points year-over-year to 33.4% of sales. Management noted improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced an acquisition of RealSense, the market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional $106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80–90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex as a key player in the expanding Physical AI and robotics perception market.

MillerKnoll beat FQ1 EPS estimates with 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents, and notably would have beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, implying underlying EPS of 42 cents. Sales disappointed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million versus the Street's $943.2 million, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed to $3.88–4.03 billion from $3.93–4.13 billion, while the EPS band was held unchanged at $1.85–2.15.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO, effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings extensive CFO experience from Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. The leadership change is a straightforward management transition with no immediate financial impact flagged.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS with 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents, as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% against the Street's 13.85% estimate, hurt by rising material costs and a difficult consumer macro backdrop. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflation straining household budgets and keeping retail soft. Bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost reduction actions underway, and a backlog surge of roughly 75% year-over-year in North American towable RVs, though the company declined to provide formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall.

Viking Therapeutics shares spiked in pre-market trading after the company reported positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. The strong efficacy data positions VK2735 as a competitive entry in the high-stakes obesity and metabolic disease drug market. This is a significant positive catalyst for the stock given the enormous commercial opportunity in the GLP-1 space.

tts_summary:
Good morning. This is a company-specific earnings note for Tuesday September 22nd, focused entirely on before-the-open results and news — there is no broad macro or rates commentary in this particular note, so let's go straight to the names.

Starting with AutoZone. The auto parts retailer posted a fiscal fourth quarter earnings beat — $56.05 versus the Street at $54.03 — but the quality was poor. The outperformance was essentially manufactured by tariff refunds adding 145 basis points to gross margins and a non-cash LIFO benefit adding another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the print looks much worse. Domestic comps came in at plus 1.6% versus the Street's plus 3.1% — a meaningful miss — and the operating expense ratio worsened by 100 basis points year-over-year. Management did note improving sales linearity in the back half of the quarter and expressed confidence for fiscal 2027, but this is a mixed-to-cautious read overall.

Next, Cognex announced it is acquiring RealSense — the market leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI — for roughly $500 million upfront plus another $106 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80 to $90 million in revenue, growing more than 50% year-over-year. This is a strategic offensive move into Physical AI and robotics — a bullish development for Cognex's long-term positioning.

MillerKnoll delivered a solid fiscal first quarter beat — 53 cents versus the Street's 36 cents — and importantly, even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, earnings still beat at 42 cents. That's clean quality. Sales were soft though, down 3.3% organically and missing the Street, and fiscal 2027 revenue guidance was trimmed modestly. EPS guidance was left unchanged. Mixed read — good earnings quality, softer top line.

THOR Industries missed. Fiscal fourth quarter EPS came in at 78 cents versus the Street's 87 cents. Gross margins were the culprit, falling 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4% as material costs surged. Management's tone was cautious — citing stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation pressuring consumers. The company won't give formal fiscal 2027 guidance until later in the fall. There were some offsets — dealer inventory is healthy, structural cost actions are underway, and the North American towable RV backlog surged roughly 75% year-over-year — but the headline read is bearish.

Finally, the standout mover this morning is Viking Therapeutics. Shares are spiking pre-market after the company reported 22% weight loss results from its GLP-1 drug trial. That is a very strong efficacy number in the obesity drug space, and it puts Viking firmly on the map as a competitive threat in one of the most commercially important drug categories in medicine right now. Clearly bullish.

Bottom line for today: no broad market directional signal in this note — it is purely a company-specific earnings morning. Watch Viking for momentum in the GLP-1 and biotech space, and treat AutoZone's beat with skepticism given the low quality of the earnings drivers.
